C2.passage: It has become fashionable to lament the decline of attention, as though concentration were a finite resource being steadily depleted by technology. Attention has never been a reservoir; it is closer to a negotiation, continuously renewed, between what the world offers and what we have trained ourselves to want. The complaint that we cannot concentrate is, more often than not, a complaint that we have not decided what is worth concentrating on — a failure of commitment dressed up as a failure of capacity.
